HasUponPickupEffect.rationale: Matches PreciseScissors.cs:14. Ancient rarity already makes the relic untradable through the other clause of Relic.is_tradable (relics/base.py:134-136), so the flag is belt-and-braces here, exactly as in the source.

AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. The relic's own arithmetic is faithful -- one removable deck card chosen and removed, executed at b12-cutters (deck 10 -> 9) with the candidate filter matching CardModel.IsRemovable (guard N1) -- but the removal goes through a bare `deck.remove` instead of the game's CardPileCmd.RemoveFromDeck, which drops the Hook.BeforeCardRemoved dispatch that verb exists to make (G1).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): `Hook.BeforeCardRemoved` has NO sim dispatch anywhere, so removing a Spoils Map leaves its map quest armed and the treasure node still pays 600 gold
guards.issue: MECHANISM: PreciseScissors.cs:22 calls `await CardPileCmd.RemoveFromDeck(item)`, which fires `await Hook.BeforeCardRemoved(card.Owner.RunState, card)` BEFORE unlinking the card (src/Core/Commands/CardPileCmd.cs:61). `grep -rn 'before_card_removed' sts2_rl/` returns ZERO hits -- neither a Relic base method nor a dispatcher -- and RunState.remove_cards (run.py:356-358) is a bare `for card in cards: self.deck.remove(card)`. The whole decompiled game has exactly ONE implementer of the hook, SpoilsMap.BeforeCardRemoved (src/Core/Models/Cards/SpoilsMap.cs:100-115), which calls `Map.GetPoint(SpoilsCoord)?.RemoveQuest(this)` -- so removing a Spoils Map from the deck is what un-arms its treasure-node payout. The sim's port substitutes an `_active_in` deck-membership test (cards/spoils_map.py:46-49) for the map-GENERATION hooks, but the payout path does not consult it: RunState._complete_map_point_quests (run.py:1052-1058) iterates `point.quests` and calls on_quest_complete with no deck check, and nothing removes the marker that after_map_generated added (cards/spoils_map.py:89-95). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b12.py b12-cardremoved): with a Spoils Map in the act-2 deck, entering the marked treasure node pays 600 gold BOTH when the card is still in the deck and when it has been removed (in_deck=False, marker still present, gold 99 -> 699). C# pays nothing in the second case. Both sides ported and obtainable: Spoils Map is granted by the ported event The Legends Were True (events/the_legends_were_true.py), it is NOT eternal so it passes CardModel.IsRemovable and appears in run.removable_cards() (executed), and FromDeckForRemoval -- unlike FromDeckForTransformation (CardSelectCmd.cs:487) -- does NOT exclude Quest cards, so the game will offer it on the removal screen too. This is a CROSS-RELIC finding: relic/precarious_shears and relic/preserved_fog in this same batch take the identical path, as does every other deck-removal site in the sim (the merchant's card-removal service, Magic Pot). Reported as a candidate pool-wide shape in .superpowers/sdd/relic-batch-12-lessons.md. NOTE per binding rule 7: CardPileCmd.cs, SpoilsMap.cs, CardSelectCmd.cs, run.py, cards/spoils_map.py and events/the_legends_were_true.py are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: the candidate filter -- `FromDeckForRemoval` takes `c.IsRemovable` (CardSelectCmd.cs:621-625) vs `run.removable_cards()`
guards.rationale: CardModel.IsRemovable is `!Keywords.Contains(CardKeyword.Eternal)` (src/Core/Models/CardModel.cs:737) and RunState.removable_cards is `[c for c in self.deck if not c.eternal]` (run.py:360-362), whose own docstring cites the same source line -- one clause, same clause. The `filter` parameter FromDeckForRemoval accepts is unused by this relic (Pomander's sibling Magic Pot is the source's example of a caller that supplies one). The sorting order C# applies -- curses first, via `(c.Type != CardType.Curse) ? deck.IndexOf(c) : -999999999` (CardSelectCmd.cs:624) -- is the removal screen's display order and does not constrain the selection, which is a player choice on both sides; the sim's default uniform-random fallback in select_cards (run.py:388-390) is a policy stand-in, not a fidelity claim. NOTE per binding rule 7: CardSelectCmd.cs, CardModel.cs and run.py are not hashed here.

CardsVar(1) (PreciseScissors.cs:16) is the pinned non-ascension value -- no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file -- and the sim's literal 1 matches; checked against the C# rather than the port's docstring per PROMPT.md bug class 19, since this port names no constant of its own (unlike its siblings precarious_shears.py:14 and preserved_fog.py:15, which do). MinSelect == MaxSelect == 1 makes RequireManualConfirmation false (src/Core/CardSelection/CardSelectorPrefs.cs:62-77), so a deck with one removable card is auto-taken -- and RunState.select_cards clamps to `min(count, len(candidates))` and returns [] on an empty list (run.py:371-390), which is the same behaviour including the degenerate case. EXECUTED (b12-cutters): deck 10 -> 9. NOTE per binding rule 7: CardSelectorPrefs.cs and run.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: `FromDeckGeneric` returns an empty selection when `player.Creature.IsDead` (CardSelectCmd.cs:640-643); the sim has no such check
guards.rationale: Structurally satisfied: RunState.add_relic is only reached from a reward/event/shop path the driver runs while the player is alive, and RunState.heal / lose_hp cannot fire between add_relic and after_obtained (run.py:546-552 is a two-statement body). Recorded rather than skipped because the same C# guard IS load-bearing for the sibling relic/precarious_shears, which deals 16 damage in the same handler and can therefore kill -- there the death test would matter if the source removed cards after damaging instead of before. Rule 5: this is a structural argument about the call site, not an unexecuted claim about a value never occurring. NOTE per binding rule 7: CardSelectCmd.cs and run.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N4: the RemoveSelectionPrompt LocString, the removal tween and NCard preview (CardPileCmd.cs:63-71)
guards.rationale: Prompt text, the card-fly-away animation and the preview container are presentation only; the sim has no UI.
